title: 2006 AMC 12A Problem 16
statement: Circles with centers \(A\) and \(B\) have radii \(3\) and \(8,\) respectively. A common internal tangent intersects the circles at \(C\) and \(D,\) respectively. Lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect at \(E,\) and \(AE = 5.\) What is \(CD?\)

solutions.text:
The radii satisfy \(AC \perp CD\) and \(BD \perp CD.\) By the Pythagorean theorem, \(CE = \sqrt{5^2 - 3^2} = 4.\)

Since \(\triangle ACE \sim \triangle BDE,\) we get \(\tfrac{DE}{CE} = \tfrac{BD}{AC} = \tfrac{8}{3},\) so \(DE = 4 \cdot \tfrac{8}{3} = \tfrac{32}{3}.\) Then \[ \begin{gathered} CD = CE + DE \\ = 4 + \frac{32}{3} \\ = \frac{44}{3}. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Radii \(AC\) and \(BD\) are perpendicular to the tangent, so \(\triangle ACE \sim \triangle BDE\)
